title: The Spark Artifact holds unresolved parameters as explicit forward references to future iterations
content:
A recurring formula appears wherever a value is not yet settled: "The specific `RateLimitID`(s) for this conduit's inflow and outflow will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.3.4.2.1.2.3, .3.5.1.1.2.3, .3.6.1.1.2.3, .4.2.1.2.3, .4.3.1.1.2.3). The same phrasing is used for individual parameters — the Blackrock instance's outflow `maxAmount` and `slope` are each "specified in a future iteration" (A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.4.1.1.2.4.2) — and the Robinhood Chain take and transferAssets limits are simply `TBD`, one annotated "(not specified in the proposal)" (.3.5.1.1.4.2.3).

The pattern is worth naming because of what it rules out. The Artifact does not omit unsettled parameters, does not guess them, and does not block the instance's registration on them. It writes down the *absence* in the slot where the value belongs.

This makes incompleteness a first-class, greppable state. A reviewer can enumerate exactly which controls are unspecified across the portfolio, and the annotation "not specified in the proposal" even preserves *why* — the governance proposal that authorized the instance never set the value.

The trade-off is that a governance artifact whose control parameters are legitimately blank cannot be read as a complete specification of risk limits. Its authority is over what it states; for the blanks, the operative constraint lives somewhere else or nowhere at all.
description: Rate Limit IDs and rate limit values repeatedly read 'will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact' or TBD, making the Artifact a living registry with declared incompleteness.
